SXM1: Liv = love. Gurmukhi = by way of the Guru. Samaliai = ought to be remembered, ought to be settled in the heart.
(But what is in the being's power?) Prabhu Himself gives the gift of His own love. Taking the Guru's shelter, one ought to keep remembering Him.
He Himself is the love, and He Himself is the embrace; the Gurmukh contemplates Him forever.
His love, He Himself makes man embrace. By Guru's grace, ever remember you the such Lord.
But that Parmeshvar Himself attaches His own love; therefore, having become a gurmukh, let us keep cherishing that Vahiguru always.
XR8Y: Nanak says, (if spiritual bliss is needed then) so great a Datar Prabhu ought never to be forgotten. ||28||
Says Nanak, why forget such a Great Giver from the mind? ||28||
Says Nanak, why should we from our mind forget that such a great Beneficent Lord?
Sri Guru Ji says: why should so great a Giver be forgotten from the mind — the sense being, let us keep remembering Him. ||28||
G8GB: Udar = the mother's belly. Bahari = in the world.
As there is fire within the mother's womb, so outside in the world Maya is (a cause of pain).
As is the fire within the womb, so is Maya outside.
As is the fire of womb within, so is the fire of mammon (Maya) without.
As the fire is in the mother's womb, so Maya, of the form of that same fire, burns the one who has come out.
Y1WZ: Maya and fire are just alike; the Creator has set going such a play.
The fire of Maya is one and the same; the Creator has staged this play.
The fires of worldly valuable and of the womb are all the same. The Creator has set agoing this play.
Maya and fire, these are in every way alike. From the beginning Parmeshvar has set going this very play.
M74D: Ja tisu bhana = when it pleased that Prabhu. Parvari = in the family. Bhala bhaia = began to seem dear.
When it is Parmatma's will the being is born, and seems dear within the family.
According to His Will, the child is born, and the family is very pleased.
When it pleases His, then is the child born and the family is well pleased.
When it pleased that Vahiguru, then he was born; and to the family his being born seemed good.
S1WY: Chhurhki = came to an end, snapped. Amaru = command. Amaru vartaia = set its command going, took hold.
(The family cherish that newborn child, and caught in this affection his) thread of love (with Prabhu's feet) snaps; the craving of Maya fastens upon him; Maya establishes its own force (over him).
Love for the Lord wears off, and the child becomes attached to desires; the script of Maya runs its course.
The Lord's Love departs, greed attaches to the child and mammon's writ begins to run.
When his attention slipped away from Parmeshvar, then Maya set its own command going, and then the craving for possessions took hold.
4EN8: Jitu = through which. Bhau duja = love of another than Prabhu.

Maya is of just this kind, that through it God is forgotten, attachment (to the world) is produced, and love for other and other (than God) springs up. (Then in such a state, where is spiritual bliss to come from?)
This is Maya, by which the Lord is forgotten; emotional attachment and love of duality well up.
Such is this mammon, by which the Lord is forgotten, worldly love wells up and one is attached to the love of another.

This very Maya it is, through which Hari may be forgotten and moh be produced — that moh which has attached duality to the being; the sense being, it is known by way of its effect, there is no other colour or form to it.
4AX7: Nanak says, those men whose thread of love stays joined to Prabhu's feet by the Guru's grace obtain (spiritual bliss) while moving about within Maya itself. ||29||
Says Nanak, by Guru's Grace, those who enshrine love for the Lord find Him, in the midst of Maya. ||29||
Says Nanak, they, who enshrine love for the Lord, by Guru's grace, obtain the Lord in the midst of mammon.
Sri Guru Ji says: those whose love has become fixed upon Hari by the mercy of the Gurus, they have obtained Prabhu while living in the very midst of Maya. ||29||
66A2: Amulaku = that which cannot be had for any price.
(Until union with Parmatma comes about, bliss cannot be enjoyed; but) a price cannot be set upon Prabhu — Parmatma cannot be had for any price (of wealth or the like).
The Lord Himself is priceless; His worth cannot be estimated.
Himself the Lord is invaluable, His price can be ascertained not.
Hari Himself is priceless; for this very reason His price is not found.
33YW: Muli = with a price, by paying a price. Kisai vitahu = from any person at all. Villai = wearing oneself out. Rahe = gave up, grew weary, were defeated.
Beings have worn themselves out and given up; to no one has Parmatma come by the paying of a price (of wealth or the like).
His worth cannot be estimated, even though people have grown weary of trying.
His price cannot be ascertained by anyone, though people have been wailing for that.
From no one (vitahu) is the price found; very many people have been left wailing — the sense being, they have exhausted every effort.
8PGN: (Yes,) if such a Guru be met (on meeting whom self-regard departs from within a man), then one's head should be offered up before that Guru (one's own self should be surrendered),
If you meet such a True Guru, offer your head to Him; your selfishness and conceit will be eradicated from within.
If you meet such a True Guru, who will dispel your self-conceit from within you, entrust you your head to him.

If such a Satiguru be met — the sense being, such as the Ved describes, that is to say, one learned in Brahm and established in Brahm — then let us surrender the head to him, and self-regard will depart from the mind.
6BAF: Jis da = whose creation. Jiu = the being. Mani = in the mind.
(and on meeting which Guru) the being stays joined at the feet of that Hari whose creation he is, and that Hari comes to dwell within his mind.
Your soul belongs to Him; remain united with Him, and the Lord will come to dwell in your mind.
Thus shall you remain united with Him, who owns your soul and God shall come to abide in your mind.
Hari Himself comes to dwell in the mind, and then this being remains merged with Him whose being he was, made separate from Himself.
UYFE: Palai pai = joins to (the Guru's) hem ||30||
O Nanak! A price cannot be set upon Parmatma (He is not had for any price); but the fortunes of those awaken to whom Parmatma joins (the Guru's) hem (they enjoy spiritual bliss). ||30||
The Lord Himself is priceless; very fortunate are those, O Nanak, who attain to the Lord. ||30||
God Himself is priceless. Fortunate are they, O Nanak, who attain to the Lord.
Hari Himself is priceless. Great are the fortunes of those, says Sri Guru Ji, in whose (palai) antahkaran He (pai) comes to be found. ||30||
T5F2: Rasi = the capital of wealth for carrying on trade. Vanjara = one who trades.
The Nam of Parmatma is my capital and my mind has become the trader.
The Lord is my capital; my mind is the merchant.
The Lord is my capital-stock and my mind is the merchant.
This mind of mine is the trader, and faith in the Nam of Hari is my capital.
BALT: Satigur te jani = obtained recognition from the Guru.
From my own Guru understanding has come to me that (for earning the profit of spiritual bliss) the Nam of Parmatma alone can be my capital; my mind has become the trader (in this trade).
The Lord is my capital, and my mind is the merchant; through the True Guru, I know my capital.
God is my capital and my mind is the merchant. Through the True Guru, I have known my capital.
Faith in Hari is my capital and my mind is the trader; but the capital in the form of faith was known from the Satigurus.
USCW: Jiahu = from the heart, with full love. Dihari = every day.
You too, remember the Nam of Hari always with love, and earn the profit (of spiritual bliss) every day.
Meditate continually on the Lord, Har, Har, O my soul, and you shall collect your profits daily.
Ever utter you the Lord's Name O my soul and you shall daily gain profit.
O being! You too repeat the Hari Hari Nam daily, and again (dihari) day by day earn this very profit.
Q9HT: This wealth (of the Hari-Nam, of spiritual bliss) is obtained only by those to whom Prabhu Himself is pleased to give it.
This wealth is obtained by those who are pleasing to the Lord's Will.
They, who are pleasing to their God, attain to this wealth.
This wealth in the form of Hari has been obtained by those whom Hari Himself has (bhana) desired.
BV30: Nanak says, the Nam of Parmatma has become my capital (and now by the Guru's grace I earn the profit of spiritual bliss). ||31||
Says Nanak, the Lord is my capital, and my mind is the merchant. ||31||
Says Nanak, God is my stock-in-trade and my soul is the trader.
Sri Guru Ji says: Hari indeed is my capital, and my mind has become the trader. ||31||
BLCS: E rasna = O (my) tongue! An rasi = in other and other relish. Rachi rahi = you are engrossed. Pias = the craving for relishes.
O (my) tongue! You are engrossed in other and other relishes; (in this way) your craving for relishes cannot be removed.
O my tongue, you are engrossed in other tastes, but your thirsty desire is not quenched.
O my tongue, you are engrossed in other relishes. Your thirst departs not.
O my tongue! You are engrossed in (an) other relishes; from this alone your thirst does not depart.
UN2J: Horatu kitai = from any other place. Palai na pai = is not obtained.
So long as the bliss of the simran of Parmatma is not obtained, the craving for relishes cannot be effaced from any other place.
Your thirst shall not be quenched by any means, until you attain the subtle essence of the Lord.
Your thirst shall not depart by any means, until you attainest to the Lord's elixir.
(Jicharu) So long as the relish of Hari does not fall into your lap, until then your trishna does not depart by any other means.
9YRZ: That man who obtains the bliss of Parmatma's Nam, who begins to enjoy the relish of the simran of Hari — the craving of Maya cannot touch him.
If you do obtain the subtle essence of the Lord, and drink in this essence of the Lord, you shall not be troubled by desire again.
If you obtain the Lord's elixir and drink the Lord's elixir, thirst shall not again affect you.
If, obtaining the relish of Hari, he holds it in the (palai) antahkaran, and drinks that relish of Hari — the sense being, repeats it — then trishna will never come and fasten upon him again.
323D: But this bliss of the Hari-Nam is had by Prabhu's mercy — it is had by him whom the Guru meets.
This subtle essence of the Lord is obtained by good karma, when one comes to meet with the True Guru.
By God's grace, this elixir of God is obtained by him, whom the True Guru comes to meet.
He to whom, by the mercy of that Parmeshvar, the Satigurus come and are met — that man then obtains this which is the relish of Hari.
A6T2: Hori an ras = all the other relishes. Sabhi = all. Man = in the mind ||32||
Nanak says, when the bliss of the simran of Hari comes to dwell in the mind, then all other and other cravings are forgotten. ||32||
Says Nanak, all other tastes and essences are forgotten, when the Lord comes to dwell within the mind. ||32||
Says Nanak, when the Lord comes to abide in man's mind, he forgets all other relishes.
Sri Guru Ji says: all the other relishes of duality, or (anras) bad relishes, are forgotten when the relish of Hari comes to dwell in the mind. ||32||
H0V6: O my body! (You seek bliss among the things of the world, but the spring of bliss is Parmatma, who dwells within you.) You came into the world only when Hari placed His own light within you.
O my body, the Lord infused His Light into you, and then you came into the world.
O my body! God placed His Light into you and then you didst come into this world.
O my body! When Hari placed the light within you, then you came into this world.
8RG4: (Know this for certain, that) when Parmatma placed His own light within you, then you were born into the world.
The Lord infused His Light into you, and then you came into the world.
The Lord put His Light into you and then didst you come in this world.
When Hari placed His own sat within you, then you came into the world.
Y8HW: Jiu = the being. Upai = having created. Jagatu dikhaia = sends the being into the world.

That Parmatma who creates the being and sends him into the world is Himself its mother and Himself its father. (Prabhu Himself, like parents, gives the being every kind of happiness; the giver of happiness and bliss is Prabhu Himself. But the being looks for bliss in the world, among the things of Maya.)
The Lord Himself is your mother, and He Himself is your father; He created the created beings, and revealed the world to them.
God Himself is the Mother and Himself the Father, Who creating man has shown him the world.
Hari Himself is of the form of the mother and Hari Himself is of the form of the father, He who, O being! having brought you into being, showed you this world.
F6PW: When by the Guru's mercy knowledge comes to the being, then he understands that this world is only a play, and then the world appears to him as (a conjuror's) show (lasting spiritual bliss cannot lie in it).
By Guru's Grace, some understand, and then it's a show; it seems like just a show.
When one realises the reality, by Guru's grace, then to him this world is a show and appears to be but a show.

The world, which is (chalatu) a wonder — that is, like a conjuror's trick — was appearing as real; and when by the Gurus' grace Parmesar was known, then this whole thing appeared as the conjuror's (chalatu) sleight; the sense being, the world was known to be false.
D4YY: Mulu rachia = laid the foundation. Jini = by which (Parmatma) ||33||
Nanak says, O my body! When Prabhu laid the foundation of the world's creation and placed His own light within you, then you were born into the world. ||33||
Says Nanak, He laid the foundation of the Universe, and infused His Light, and then you came into the world. ||33||
Says Nanak, the Lord laid the foundation of the universe, infused His Light within your body and then you calmest into the world.
Sri Guru Ji says: the root of the creation, which is agian — by that He first fashioned the world; and again He placed His own (joti) sat within your body, then you came into the world. ||33||
FFNC: Chau = bliss. Prabh agamu = Prabhu's coming.
I have heard of the coming of Prabhu-Husband upon my own heart-bed (I have felt that Prabhu has come to dwell within my heart, and now) bliss has arisen in my mind.
My mind has become joyful, hearing of God's coming.
My soul is in ecstasy, hearing the coming of my Lord.
When the (agamu) coming of Prabhu — that is, His becoming manifest — was heard, then great gladness arose in the mind.
14FA: Sakhi = O friend! O soul! Mangalu = a song of joy, the song of Prabhu's praise. Grihu = the heart-house. Mandaru = Prabhu's dwelling-place.
O my soul! This heart-house of mine has become the dwelling-place of Prabhu-Husband; now sing the song of Prabhu's praise.
Sing the songs of joy to welcome the Lord, O my companions; my household has become the Lord's Mansion.
Sing you, the songs of rejoicing to welcome my Lord, O my mates. My house has now become my Lord's mansion.
O friend in the form of a sant! Sing the mangal of Hari. Those who have sung it, their whole (grihu) body and (mandaru) heart have been made resplendent.
FJDA: Na viapae = does not press, does not exert its weight.
O soul! Keep singing always the song of Prabhu's greatness; (in this way) no anxiety and no sorrow can exert its force.
Sing continually the songs of joy to welcome the Lord, O my companions, and sorrow and suffering will not afflict you.
Ever sing you the songs of welcome to my God, O mates, and sorrow and suffering shall cling you not.
Sing the mangal of Hari daily, O friend! By this alone sorrow and pain will not press upon you.
DLHV: Sabhage = fortunate. Japae = has become visible.
Those days are fortunate when (the brow) rests upon the Guru's feet; the beloved Husband-Prabhu becomes visible (within the heart).
Blessed is that day, when I am attached to the Guru's feet and meditate on my Husband Lord.
Very fortunate is the day when I am attached to the Guru's feet and reflect on my beloved.
We have fallen at the feet of the Gurus; most fortunate days have come; we repeat Him who is our own husband.
WBAJ: Anahat = unbroken. Anahat bani = the unbroken current of praise. Sabadi = through the shabad.
Through the Guru's shabad acquaintance comes about with the unbroken current of praise; Prabhu's Nam is obtained; the bliss of union with Prabhu is enjoyed.
I have come to know the unstruck sound current and the Word of the Guru's Shabad; I enjoy the sublime essence of the Lord, the Lord's Name.
By Guru's instruction, I have realised the unbeaten music and enjoy the Divine relish of God's Name.
The unbroken bani of the Guru's updesh has been known — the sense being, it has been reflected upon without interruption — and from this alone we enjoy the relish of the Hari Hari Nam.

6QZ1: Nanak says, (O soul! Sing the song of joy) Prabhu who is capable of doing all things has Himself come and met me. ||34||
Says Nanak, God Himself has met me; He is the Doer, the Cause of causes. ||34||
Says Nanak, the Lord Himself, who is potent to do all deeds, has met me.
Sri Guru Ji says: Prabhu Himself has met, He who is capable of making Brahma and the rest. ||34||
ZJ5T: Kia karam = which works? Only other and other works.
O my body! Having taken birth in this world, you went on doing only other and other works.
O my body, why have you come into this world? What actions have you committed?
O my body, what deed hats you done by coming into this world?
O my body! Having come into this age, what good karam have you earned?
W964: Since the time you came into the world, you went on doing only other and other works (apart from the simran of Prabhu).
And what actions have you committed, O my body, since you came into this world?
What deed hats you done, O body of mine, since you came into this world?
What karam have you earned, O body! since you came into the world.
41X4: Jini hari = which Hari. Tera rachanu rachia = created you. Mani = in the mind.
That Hari who created you — Him you did not settle within your own mind (you never joined yourself to His remembrance).
The Lord who formed your form - you have not enshrined that Lord in your mind.
He, the Lord, who didst make your make; That Lord you have not enshrined in your mind.
That Hari who made this (rachanu) fashioning of yours — that Hari you have not settled in the mind; then all your other works are in vain.
Q645: (But, O body! What is even in your power?) That man whose sanskars of deeds done in the past come to light — by the Guru's grace Parmatma dwells within his mind (he alone joins himself to the simran of Hari).
By Guru's Grace, the Lord abides within the mind, and one's pre-ordained destiny is fulfilled.
By Guru's grace, the Lord abides within my mind and I obtain what is pre-destined for me.
Those in whose mind Hari has come to dwell by the mercy of the Gurus, they have obtained it just according to the writ written beforehand.
KHSD: Jini = which man. Parvanu = accepted, fruitful ||35||
Nanak says, that man who has joined his chit to the Guru's feet — his body becomes fruitful (he accomplishes the purpose for which it was made). ||35||
Says Nanak, this body is adorned and honored, when one's consciousness is focused on the True Guru. ||35||
Says Nanak, this body of him, who attaches his mind to the True Guru, becomes acceptable.
Sri Guru Ji says: their body has become accepted who have joined their chit to the Satigurus. ||35||
LWNF: O my eyes! Parmatma has set His own light within you (that is why you are able to see); wherever you look, behold Parmatma alone.
O my eyes, the Lord has infused His Light into you; do not look upon any other than the Lord.
O my yes, God has infused light in you. Without the Lord, see you not another, therefore.
O my eyes! Hari has placed within you the light whose form is illumination; therefore see none other than Hari.
15NN: Nihalia = behold. Nadari = with the sight, with the eyes.
Let no other stranger be seen apart from Parmatma; behold Hari with your sight.
Do not look upon any other than the Lord; the Lord alone is worthy of beholding.
Save the Lord, see you not any other. The Merciful Master-Lord alone is worthy of beholding.
See none other than Hari. Hari is (nadari) the one who shows mercy; Him alone one ought to (nihalia) behold — the sense being, behold Hari.
WA02: Visu = vishv, the whole. Nadari aia = is seen.
(O eyes!) This whole world that you are seeing is Prabhu's own form; it is Prabhu's own form that is being seen.
This whole world which you see is the image of the Lord; only the image of the Lord is seen.
This entire world, which you behold is the Lord's manifestation. God's image alone is seen in it.
This (visu) entire, or poison-formed — that is, pain-giving — world that you see, all this is Hari's form now; and formerly too, to the mahatmas, this appeared as Hari's form alone.
U6WS: By the Guru's grace understanding has come to me; now when I look (all around), everywhere one Parmatma alone is seen; apart from Him there is nothing else.
By Guru's Grace, I understand, and I see only the One Lord; there is no one except the Lord.
By Guru's grace, when I realise the reality, I perceive but one God. Without the Lord, there is not any other.
(Gur parsadi) By the grace of the Gurus it has been known; when I looked, then it is the one Vahiguru alone; and again, apart from Hari there is none other.
AG7C: Andh = blind. Se = were. Dib = (divya) shining, luminous. Dristi = sight ||36||

Nanak says, (before meeting the Guru) these eyes were (in truth) blind; when the Guru was met, light came into them (they began to see Parmatma everywhere. This very darshan is the root of bliss). ||36||
Says Nanak, these eyes were blind; but meeting the True Guru, they became all-seeing. ||36||
Says Nanak, these eyes were blind, on meeting the True Guru, they have become omniscient.

Sri Guru Ji says: these gross eyes were blind; by the meeting with the Satigurus the dib-drishti, the sight of the gian, has come about — the sense being, they see all as the form of Parmeshvar. ||36||
12QN: O my ears! (Parmatma) has made you for hearing the bani of Parmatma's praise,
O my ears, you were created only to hear the Truth.
O cars of mine, you were sent to hear the True Name.
O my ears! You have been (pathae) sent by the true Hari for the hearing of His own Nam.
1K3K: Sachai = the ever-abiding Prabhu. Sariri = in the body. Sati bani = the bani of the praise of the ever-abiding Prabhu.
hear the bani of Parmatma's praise; the ever-abiding Creator has made you for hearing just this, and has set you in this body.
To hear the Truth, you were created and attached to the body; listen to the True Bani.
You were sent and attached to the body to hear the True Name. Hear you, the True word;
You who have been attached to the body have been sent for the hearing of the true Nam; therefore hear the (bani) updesh of the True-Formed One.
BSJX: Jitu = through which. Jitu suni = by the hearing of which. Rasi = in bliss. Haria = blossoming, filled with bliss. Rasna = tongue.
By the hearing of this bani of praise, body and mind become filled with bliss, and the tongue is engrossed in bliss.
Hearing it, the mind and body are rejuvenated, and the tongue is absorbed in Ambrosial Nectar.
Hearing which the soul and body are revived and the tongue is absorbed in the Name-Nectar.
By the hearing of which the mind and body of the seekers have blossomed, and the tongue has become absorbed in the relish.
YT8B: The ever-abiding Parmatma is of a wondrous form; no mark or sign of Him can be told; it cannot be said what He is like.
The True Lord is unseen and wondrous; His state cannot be described.
The true Lord is Invisible and Wondrous. His state can, be told not.
He who is the True One, the unseen, of wondrous form — His state indeed cannot be told.
DTNR: Amrit = that which gives spiritual bliss ||37||

(By the speaking and hearing of His virtues this alone is gained, that a man obtains spiritual bliss; and therefore) Nanak says, keep hearing the Nam that gives spiritual bliss, and you will become pure; Parmatma has sent (made) you for hearing just this. ||37||
Says Nanak, listen to the Ambrosial Naam and become holy; you were created only to hear the Truth. ||37||
Says Nanak, hear you the Nectar-Name and become immaculate. You O ears, were sent to hear the True Name.
Sri Guru Ji says: hear the amrit of the Nam and you will become pure, because you have been sent for the hearing of the true Nam alone. ||37||
FJM8: Jiu = the soul. Gupha = the body. Pavanu vaja vajaia = sounded the instrument of the breath, gave the power of speech.
Parmatma, having settled the soul within the body-cave, gave the being the power of speech.
The Lord placed the soul to the cave of the body, and blew the breath of life into the musical instrument of the body.
Placing the soul in the body cave, the Lord began to blow the musical instrument of breath into it.

Beloved Hari, having placed the soul within the cave that is the body, has sounded within it the instrument of the breath — the sense being, by the prana-breath He has caused all activity to be carried on.
JTHC: Nau duare = the nine openings: 1 mouth, 2 ears, 2 eyes, 2 nostrils, the anus, the organ of generation.
He gave the body the power of speech, made the nine organs — nose, ears and the rest — openly, and kept the tenth door (the brain) hidden.
He blew the breath of life into the musical instrument of the body, and revealed the nine doors; but He kept the Tenth Door hidden.
He blew the musical instrument of breath, made the nine doors manifest and the tenth He has kept concealed.
He sounded the instrument of the breath, and made the nine doors of the body (pargat) open; and again, the tenth door which there is, He kept hidden indeed.
F41Z: Dasva duar = (that is,) the brain (by means of which a man can reflect). Bhavani = faith, love.

Those whom Prabhu brought to the Guru's door and granted faith in His own Nam — to them He showed the tenth door as well (He gave them also the reflective power of simran, which is the root of spiritual bliss).
Through the Gurdwara, the Guru's Gate, some are blessed with loving faith, and the Tenth Door is revealed to them.
Through the Guru, blessing some with faith, He shows the tenth gate.

Those who have set their faith by way of the Gurus — to some such the Gurus have shown the tenth door plainly; or, the tenth, the conscious principle, which is the support of the nine, heaven and the rest.
8G4V: Tah = in that state. Anek rup nau = the Nam of the Prabhu of countless forms. Nidhi = treasure.
In that state a man obtains also that Nam of the Prabhu pervading in countless colours and forms, that store of the nine treasures, whose end cannot be found (which never runs out).
There are many images of the Lord, and the nine treasures of the Naam; His limits cannot be found.
The Lord of manifold forms and the Name's nine treasures are there. His limit can be found not.

Within it is the world of name and form, of countless kinds; and again He is the maker of the nine nidhis. Of what kind is He? That His limit is not found — the sense being, they have seen the boundless Parmesar; or, within the tenth door is everything spoken of above.
MDJQ: Nanak says, the beloved Prabhu, having settled the soul within the body-cave, gave the being the power of speech as well. ||38||
Says Nanak, the Lord placed the soul to the cave of the body, and blew the breath of life into the musical instrument of the body. ||38||
Says Nanak, putting the soul in the body-cave, the beloved Lord has blown the breath in it is a musical instrument.

Sri Guru Ji says: beloved Hari, having placed the soul within the cave that is the body, has again sounded the instrument of the breath. ||38|| ☬ This one pauri, on the greatness of the Anand bani, was uttered by the Fourth Patshahi.
R6CF: Sohila = a song of joy, a song that produces spiritual bliss, the bani of Prabhu's praise. Sachai ghari = in the ever-abiding house, in the sadh sangat.
Sing this bani of the praise of Parmatma (seated) in the sadh sangat.
Sing this true song of praise in the true home of your soul.
Sing you this true song of the Lord's praise, in the true home of your soul.
This which is the true (sohila) praise, the bani named Anand — sing it, joining together, (sachai ghari) in the sadh sangat.
EJTE: Sachu = the ever-abiding Prabhu. Gavahu = gavahi, (the satsangis) sing.
Keep singing in that satsang the bani that gives spiritual bliss, where (the gurmukhs) sing always of the ever-abiding Prabhu.
Sing the song of praise in your true home; meditate there on the True Lord forever.
Sing you the song of God's praise in the true home, where the saints ever contemplate the True Lord.
Sing this praise, or the Anand bani, in the true house, where always the dhyan of the True One alone takes place. ☬ Those who sing the sohila make their supplication in this manner:

PYPJ: Bed = the Vedas and other religious books. Nirmae = were made, became manifest.
The Vedas too were made from Oankar alone.
It is the Lord who created the Vedas.
From Oankar Parmatma the Vedas were (nirmae) brought into being.

BTWJ: Oankar = through Oankar, through the all-pervading Parmatma. Sabad = through the Shabad, by being joined to the Shabad. Udhare = (beings) were saved (from drowning).
By joining themselves to the Guru's Shabad, beings are saved from the vices of the world only with the help of that all-pervading Parmatma,
Ongkaar saves the world through the Shabad.
It is through the One Lord, that the world is saved.
By worshipping Oankar, (sabad) Brahm, beings have been saved; or, Oankar Brahm saved the (sabad) Vedas that had been stolen by the demons.
W6K3: Gurmukh = a person turned towards the Guru, those whose face stays towards the Guru.
and by walking the path the Guru has shown, they cross over the world-ocean.
It is through the Lord, that the God-conscious beings are emancipated.
Through the worship of Oankar, by way of the (gurmukh) Guru, beings have crossed the world-ocean.
DAUG: Onam akhar bicharu = the reflection on the word 'Onam' {note: the difference between the word 'akhar' in this line and the word 'akharu' in the next line is worth remembering. In 'akhar bicharu', 'akhar' is in the genitive case, meaning 'the reflection on the word'. In the next line 'akharu' is nominative singular, meaning "the Onam-word is the essence of the three worlds"}. Onam = {in the schools, teachers write the words (ओं नमः) 'Om namah' on the boys' writing boards when teaching them, which means 'salutation to Om, salutation to Parmatma'. On his first udasi, when Guru Nanak Dev ji was returning from Sangladip by way of Somnath and Dwarka, and travelled along the banks of the river Narbada to the place where the temple of Oankar stands, he saw that the people worshipped the Shiva-idol installed in the temple, taking it to be 'Oankar'. The pupils of the temple school wrote and were made to write 'Om namah' on their boards, but they too took that Shiva-idol itself to be 'Om'. Both these errors are explained in this first pauri} Om namah, salutation to Om.
(O Pandit! You write the words 'Om namah' on your pupils' boards, but you take this idol itself to be 'Om') — hear also about that great Being for whom you write the words 'Om namah'.
Listen to the Message of the Universal, Imperishable Creator Lord.
Hear you the account of the imperishable Lord, worthy of obeisance.
Hear the reflection upon Oankar, the imperishable one, who is worthy of salutation.
ZY0X: Onam akhar = that Being for whom the word 'Onam' is used. Onam akhar bicharu = the reflection on that Being for whom you are using the word 'Onam'. Tribhavan saru = the essence of the three worlds, the root of the three worlds, the creator of the whole creation. ||1||
These words 'Om namah' are for that (great Akal Purakh) who is the creator of the whole creation. ||1||
The Universal, Imperishable Creator Lord is the essence of the three worlds. ||1||
The eternal Lord is the essence of the three world.
Oankar alone is the essence in the three worlds. ||1||
RQE9: Kia likhahu = what is the gain to you in writing? There is no gain in writing. Janjal = the mere entanglements of the world.
O Pandit, listen! No (spiritual) gain can come from writing that is nothing but (argument and worldly) entanglement.
Listen, O Pandit, O religious scholar, why are you writing about worldly debates?
Hear, O pandit, why write you the worldly puzzles?
O Pandit, listen! Why do you write down actions that are of the form of bondage?
SX5K: (If you want to make your life fruitful, then) turning your face towards the Guru, write (in your own mind) the Name of Parmatma, the Master of creation. ||1||Rahau||
As Gurmukh, write only the Name of the Lord, the Lord of the World. ||1||Pause||
By Guru's grace, write you only the Name of the Lord, the cherisher of the world. Pause.
Through the Guru, write the Name of Ram, Gopal. ||1||Rahau||
FTHH: Sasai = through the letter 'sassa'. Sahaj = naturally, without any special effort. Teen bhavan = in the three worlds, in the sky, the underworld and this mortal world, in the whole world. Ik joti = the light of the one Parmatma.
The Parmatma who created this whole world without any special effort — His light is spreading through the whole world.
Sassa: He created the entire universe with ease; His One Light pervades the three worlds.
S: God created the whole world with ease, In the three worlds is the one luminous Lord.
This is the reflection on the letter sassa: the world, which is of the form of the three worlds, was all created by the (ik joti) Parmatma without effort.
TXQX: Gurmukh = one whose face is towards the Guru, a person who walks the path the Guru has shown. Vastu = the Ram Nam of Gopal. Chun lai = (the gurmukh person) picks out. Manak moti = the precious wealth of the form of Parmatma's Name.
The person who walks the path the Guru has shown receives the treasure of that Parmatma's Name; the gurmukh gathers the precious wealth of Parmatma's Name.
Become Gurmukh, and obtain the real thing; gather the gems and pearls.
Pick up you the gems and pearls of the Name and by the Guru's grace you shall obtain God, the Real commodity.

The gurmukhs who pick out the virtues — (manak) reflection, (moti) detachment and the rest — that is, those who take on virtues through the company of the holy, attain the treasure of the self in this world.
ASTY: Ant = in the end, at last (meaning, compared with all other things). Nirantar = {nir-antar} uniform, present everywhere. Sacha = ever-abiding.

That person comes to understand and reflect through (the bani of) the Satguru; reading the Satguru's bani again and again, the secret opens to him that the all-pervading Parmatma alone is, in the end, ever-abiding.
If one understands, realizes and comprehends what he reads and studies, in the end he shall realize that the True Lord dwells deep within his nucleus.
If man, understands, reflects and comprehends what he reads and peruses, he ultimately comes to realise that the True Lord is within all.

Having read the shastras again and again, those who ask the Satgurus, who are the form of Bhagvan, and then, understanding the Guru's teaching, put it into practice — to them comes the direct realisation of the true Vahiguru, who is (ant) the limit of all and (nirantar) uniform.
TAPE: Sach samale = remembers the ever-abiding Parmatma. Kacha = perishable. ||2||
The person who walks the Guru's path sees only that ever-abiding Parmatma (everywhere) and enshrines Him in his heart; apart from Parmatma, all the rest of the world appears to him perishable. ||2||
The Gurmukh sees and contemplates the True Lord; without the True Lord, the world is false. ||2||
The pious persons perceives and contemplates the True Lord With your True Lord, the world is but false.
The gurmukhs who cherish the true Name see with the eyes of reflection. What do they see? That apart from the true Vahiguru, this world of name and form is (kacha) false. ||2||
X8SS: Dharma puri = in the city of dharma, in the satsang. Dharam dhare = (the Satguru) teaches dharma. Gunkari = the one who produces virtues. Dhira = steady.

(O Pandit! Taking the Guru's refuge, write the Creator's Name on the board of your mind; He is great and boundless.) In the satsang the Satguru teaches the dharma (of remembering that Creator); (by the blessing of remembrance) the Satguru's own mind stays steady, and he produces (these) virtues in others too.
Dhadha: Those who enshrine Dharmic faith and dwell in the City of Dharma are worthy; their minds are steadfast and stable.
Dh: The meritorious men, with steadfast mind, cherish Lord's devotion in this world, the city of faith.

This is the reflection on the letter dhadha: those great souls who uphold dharma are complete in every dharma. The minds of those who bring forth virtue — that is, of those virtuous ones — are steadfast.
U93Y: Dhul = dust, the dust of the feet. Mukh mastak = on (whose) face, on (whose) forehead. Manur = burnt iron, slag.
The person on whose face and forehead the dust of the Guru's feet falls turns from useless burnt iron into gold.
Dhadha: If the dust of their feet touches one's face and forehead, he is transformed from iron into gold.
Dh: if the dust of such saints' feet alights on man's face and forehead, from iron dross he is transmuted into Gold.

Through dhadha he says: when the dust of the feet of that Parmatma falls on the forehead, the soul becomes pure; and those on whom it has fallen, though they were filthy like slag, have still become (kanchan) gold, that is, of the form of pure Brahm.
384Q: Dharnidhar = Parmatma, the support of the earth. Ajoni = the Prabhu who is free of birth. Tol = in weighing. Bol = in speech.
The Parmatma who is the support of creation, who has no rival, and who is free of birth — He alone is the Satguru's wealth; the Satguru is true and complete in his weighing and in his speech.
Blessed is the Support of the Earth; He Himself is not born; His measure and speech are perfect and True.
Blessed is He, the supporter of the earth, who Himself is unborn and whose decision and speech are true and perfect.

(Dharnidhar) the one who holds up the earth, that is, Parmesar, is blessed. And what is He like? He Himself is free of birth, His (tol) reflection is complete and His (bol) word is true; or, the saints whose wealth is Dharnidhar alone, the true one — the (tol) reflection of those saints is complete and their (bol) word is true.
MN1A: Mit = measure, extent, greatness, glory. Kai = or. Aap = all by Himself, He who has no rival. Tol bol sach pura = (meaning, the Guru's way of living is pure to the last ounce, and the Guru's word too rings wholly true). ||3||
The Creator alone knows the Creator's glory, or the heroic Satguru knows it (meaning, only the Satguru appreciates Parmatma's glory). ||3||
Only the Creator Himself knows His own extent; He alone knows the Brave Guru. ||3||
The Creator's extent, only the Creator knows, or knows the valiant Guru,
The (mit) limits of the Creator are known only to the Creator, (kai) or else to the Guru who has slain the enemies — lust and the rest — that hero knows it. ||3||
TRGU: Nyanu = the teaching given by the Guru. Duja = something other than the Guru's teaching. Bhaia = pleased (the person). Garab = in pride. Gale = rotted, sank down. Bikh = poison (which brought spiritual death).
The person who forgets the Satguru's teaching and prefers some other way of life sinks down into pride, and he eats the poison (of pride, the root of spiritual death).
In love with duality, spiritual wisdom is lost; the mortal rots away in pride, and eats poison.
Loving another, man loses Divine Knowledge, he putrefies in pride and eats poison.

The being who has been pleased by the sense of duality and has lost gyan — meaning, he has not attained gyan — sunk in pride, he has eaten the poison of the form of the sense-objects, and does not know it.
JDT6: Gur ras geet = the joy of the Guru's bani. Bad = a saying, the Guru's saying. Nahi bhavai sunia = it does not please (him) to hear it, he does not feel like listening. Gahir gambhir = the unfathomable Parmatma, the Prabhu who is master of countless virtues.

(Because of the sense of duality) that person does not like to hear the joy of the Satguru's bani and the Guru's words. That person becomes separated from Parmatma, the master of unfathomable virtues.
He thinks that the sublime essence of the Guru's song is useless, and he does not like to hear it. He loses the profound, unfathomable Lord.
The ambrosial hymn of the Guru, he deems vain and likes not to hear it, Thus loses he, the Profound and Unfathomable Lord.
The one who has not listened to the Guru's (geet) praise, spoken in the form of nectar — that is, he has lost the (gahir gambhir) Parmesar.
64PU: Gur = through the Satguru. Sach kahia = (who) remembered the ever-abiding Parmatma. Lahia = (he) has found. Man = in the mind. Tan = in the body. Sach = the ever-abiding Prabhu. Sukhaia = became dear.
The person who has remembered the ever-abiding Prabhu through the Satguru has obtained the nectar of the Name; then that Parmatma becomes dear to him in mind and body.
Through the Guru's Words of Truth, the Ambrosial Nectar is obtained, and the mind and body find joy in the True Lord.
If the mortal believes, that the Guru tells truth, he obtains Nectar and to his soul and body, the True Lord becomes pleasing.

The one to whom the Guru has spoken the teaching that is of the form of truth has received the teaching that is of the form of amrit. The truth pleases him in mind and body; that is, he worships with body and mind.
UGXQ: Gurmukh = by turning towards the Guru, through the Guru. Aape = the Prabhu Himself. ||4||
(But this is only His gift:) He Himself, placing one in the Guru's refuge, gives (the gift of remembrance), and He Himself gives the nectar of the Name to drink. ||4||
He Himself is the Gurmukh, and He Himself bestows the Ambrosial Nectar; He Himself leads us to drink it in. ||4||
The Lord Himself is the Exalted Guru. Himself he blesses man with the Nectar-Name and Himself makes him quaff this Nectar.
He Himself, becoming the Guru, gives the amrit into the mouth to drink, and He Himself, becoming the seeker, comes and drinks the amrit. ||4||
MTZH: Eko ek = only the one (Parmatma). Sabh koi = every being. Garab = pride. Viapai = keeps its hold, stays spread over.
(In a way) everyone says that there is only one Parmatma, but (over the mind on which Parmatma's Name is to be written) ego and pride keep their hold.
Everyone says that God is the One and only, but they are engrossed in egotism and pride.
Every one says that Lord is, but One, but each one is engrossed in ego and pride.
In speech, everyone says "One, only One"; but within, they are caught up in the pride of the body and the arrogance of wealth and the rest.
2MVE: Iu = (meaning,) by removing the shadow of ego and pride. Ghar mahal = the abode of Parmatma. Sinjapai = is recognised.
If a person (removing the shadow of ego and pride) recognises the one Parmatma in his own heart and in the whole creation, then in this way he comes to recognise Parmatma's abode.
Realize that the One God is inside and outside; understand this, that the Mansion of His Presence is within the home of your heart.
Let man know the one Lord within and without; Like this shall he realise the Lord's presence in his very home.
Those who recognise the One within and without — whoever hears the teaching through them (iu), in the way described above, (sivapai) recognises the (ghar mahal) true form.
647W: Dur na janahu = (O Pandit!) do not think of the Prabhu as somewhere far away. Eko = the one Prabhu alone. Sabai = all.
(O Pandit!) Parmatma is near (you) (meaning, dwelling in your heart); do not think of Him as far (from yourself). The one Parmatma alone is present in the whole creation.
God is near at hand; do not think that God is far away. The One Lord permeates the entire universe.
The Lord is near. Consider not God to be far, he alone is permeating the whole world.
Therefore do not think Him far; the all-powerful Hari is near. It is the One alone who is seen in all creation.
A6F7: Ekankaru = the all-pervading Parmatma. Samai = is present everywhere. ||5||
O Nanak! The one all-pervading Parmatma alone is contained (everywhere); there is no other apart from Him. ||5||
There in One Universal Creator Lord; there is no other at all. O Nanak, merge into the One Lord. ||5||
There is but one Lord. There is not another. Nanak, remains merged in the One Lord.
That is of the form of Oankar alone; there is no other at all. Sri Guru ji says: all creation merges into the One alone. ||5||
K8P8: Is karte kau = this Creator who dwells near (meaning, even though the Creator dwells within me). Gahi rakhau = may I hold on to, may I keep enshrined in the heart. Aphario = cannot be grasped, cannot be enshrined in the heart. Tulio na jai = cannot be weighed, His glory cannot be appreciated. Kiu = how? (meaning, not so long as 'ego and pride' are within).

(O Pandit!) Even though the Creator dwells within me, (so long as there is ego and pride within me) I cannot enshrine Him in my mind; (so long as there is ego in the mind, that Creator) cannot be enshrined in the mind, and His glory cannot be appreciated.
How can you keep the Creator under your control? He cannot be seized or measured.
This mind-actor, how can you keep under control? It is unseizable and is immeasurable.
How can I hold on to this mind, which acts and enjoys? For it is (aphario) unbendable and cannot be weighed — meaning, one moment it weighs a tola and the next a masha.
V1B2: Dewane = the one intoxicated. Jhuth = falsehood. Thagauri = the thugs' herb, a stupefying drug, a pull, a spell.
(So long as) falsehood has fed the thugs' drug to the being intoxicated with Maya,
Maya has made the mortal insane; she has administered the poisonous drug of falsehood.
Giving the intoxicating herb of falsehood, mammon has made the mortal mad.
These living beings have been made mad by Maya, and falsehood, which is of the form of vice, has slipped the thugs' drug to them.
GHPB: Lab = in craving for taste. Lobh = in greed. Muhtaj = in dependence. Ib tab phir = now and then, again and again, always.
(so long as the being) is ruined in craving, in greed and in dependence on others, so long does it sigh and sigh at every moment.
Addicted to greed and avarice, the mortal is ruined, and then later, he regrets and repents.
Becoming indigent through greed and avarice, mortal is ruined and ever grieves afterwards.
Through craving and greed they have become (muhtaj) wretched and ruined. (Ib) in the present time, (tab) at the time of death, (phir) again and again, they regret.
GUGL: Sarevai = remembers. Gat = the state of Parmatma, acquaintance with the Prabhu. Mit = the measure of Parmatma, appreciation of the Prabhu's glory. Rahai = ends. ||6||
When a person (removing ego) remembers the one Parmatma, then he comes to know Parmatma, he comes to appreciate Parmatma's glory, and his birth and death come to an end. ||6||
So serve the One Lord, and attain the state of Salvation; your comings and goings shall cease. ||6||
If man serves the one Lord, then he realises he the worth of emancipation and his comings and goings cease,

If one serves the One, then he attains the bounds of liberation; only then will a soul be freed from coming and going. ||6|| ☬ The One alone has become the form of all — this principle he now reveals:
F6EC: Eku, iku = the one Parmatma alone. Acharu = conduct, activity.

(O Pandit! Write on the board of your mind the Name of that Gopal who) alone (pervading everywhere, is doing all) the work (of the world), (who) alone (is bringing forth from Himself all) the form and colour (of the world),
The One Lord is in all actions, colors and forms.
The Unique Lord is in all deeds, colours and forms.
The one Parmatma alone is of the form of all action; all colour and form too is the One alone.
ZY8J: and (these elements of the world) — air, water and fire — are (His own) form,
He manifests in many shapes through wind, water and fire.
He works through winds, water, fire and various shapes.
He Himself is (as) of the form of air, water and fire too.
Z2NT: Eko bhavaru = one soul alone, the light of the one Parmatma alone. Bhavai = is spreading, is all-pervading. Tih loi = in the three worlds, in the whole world.
the Gopal whose light alone is spreading through the whole world.
The One Soul wanders through the three worlds.
The one soul wanders through the three worlds.
That One alone, becoming the (bhavaru) living soul, wanders through the three worlds.
LERS: The person who understands that one Parmatma (as pervading everywhere), to whom Parmatma alone is seen everywhere, receives honour and respect.
One who understands and comprehends the One Lord is honored.
If the mortal understands and perceives One God; he is blessed with honour, then.
Whoever asks the one Satguru and (sujhai) comes to direct realisation — he will have honour.
UZD4: Gian = acquaintance with Parmatma. Dhian = attention fixed on Parmatma. Le = having obtained. Samsar = even, level, of balanced life, steady, free of ego and pride.
Some person, having come to know Parmatma through the Satguru and having fixed his attention on Him, becomes one of steady life,
One who gathers in spiritual wisdom and meditation, dwells in the state of balance.
He, who gathers divine wisdom and meditation; abides in a state of evenness
Through the gyan of the Guru, whoever takes Parmatma into his meditation remains (samsar) even-minded throughout.
748M: Gurmukh = a person turned towards the Guru. Iku = the one Parmatma.
such a rare person attains that Parmatma.
How rare are those who, as Gurmukh, attain the One Lord.
Some rare One attains to the one Lord by Guru's grace.
Then some rare gurmukh takes hold of this oneness.
6PJ7: Kirpa te = with (the Prabhu's) grace. Dei = gives.
That person enjoys peace to whom the Prabhu, by His grace, gives this gift,
They alone find peace, whom the Lord blesses with His Grace.
He, whom the Lord gives through. His grace, He alone obtains peace.
Moreover, whoever He gives it to by His own grace, he too finds peace.
MBVK: Guru duarai = through the Satguru. Aakh = having told, having given counsel. ||7||
and to whom He makes (the teaching of His all-pervasiveness) heard through the Guru. ||7||
In the Gurdwara, the Guru's Door, they speak and hear of the Lord. ||7||
He, then utter and preaches the True Name, through the Guru.
But He speaks and makes it heard by the Guru's way — meaning, when the seeker is complete in the fourfold means and devoted to service, then the Guru gives him the teaching. ||7||
NE9R: Uram = {Sanskrit: urvi} the earth. Dhuram = {Sanskrit: dhumra} smoke, the sky. Ujala = light, radiance.
(O Pandit! Write on the board of your mind the Name of that Gopal) whose light shines in the earth and the sky,
His Light illuminates the ocean and the earth.
The Lord's light, illumines the ocean and the earth.
In (uram) the earth and (dhuram) the sky is the radiance of the light; or, uram dhuram — He is especially pervading the heart.
BMHH: Gur = the greatest of all. Gopal = the sustainer of the earth.
that greatest Gopal of all, who pervades the three worlds.
Throughout the three worlds, is the Guru, the Lord of the World.
The great cherisher of the worlds is contained in the three worlds.
It is that very light, Gur Gopal, whose radiance is in the three worlds.
280K: Ugvia = having become manifest. Asarupu = His own form.
The one to whom that Gopal, by His grace, becoming manifest (through the Guru), shows His own (all-pervading) form,
The Lord reveals His various forms;
When such Divine comprehension wells up, then God shows his vision,
When such gyan dawns in the soul, then He shows (as) His own form.
J9VL: Ghar aavai = (that person) is saved from wandering, becomes steady. Ghar = in the home.
that person (saved from wandering) becomes steady within himself.
granting His Grace, He enters the home of the heart.
and mercifully enters into the mortal's own house.
When by His grace He comes into the heart of His own seeker — meaning, He is directly realised.
CULN: Unav = bending down, leaning close. Nijhar dhara = in a steady downpour, unbroken.
The Prabhu who makes the world beautiful draws near (in the heart of that person) and rains down (His praise) in a steady downpour,
The clouds hang low, and the rain is pouring down.
Descending low, the ambrosial rain is incessantly falling.
(Unav) bending down — meaning, becoming compassionate — the cloud in the form of the Guru rains down the unbroken stream of amrit that is the teaching.
Z534: Utam sabad = through the Guru's supreme Shabad. Savaranhara = Parmatma, who makes the world beautiful.
through the Satguru's supreme Shabad, that person (comes to know of the One who adorns the world) —
The Lord embellishes and exalts with the Sublime Word of the Shabad.
The sublime Gurbani, embellishes the mortal.
That supreme (sabad) teaching of the Guru is what adorns the Sikh.
2V6H: Is eke ka = of the one Prabhu who adorns the world. Bheu = (this) secret (that).
he comes to know this secret of this Prabhu,
One who knows the mystery of the One God,
He, who knows the secret of this one God,
The one who knows the secret of this one Parmeshvar —
6MF1: Aape = Himself alone. Deu = the one who gives light. ||8||
that the Prabhu Himself is the creator of the whole world, and He Himself gives it light (with His own light) (meaning, the Prabhu Himself teaches this world the way of life). ||8||
is Himself the Creator, Himself the Divine Lord. ||8||
is himself the Creator and Himself the Luminous Lord.
He Himself is the creator, and He Himself is (deu) of the form of light. ||8||
9BEK: Suru = the sun, light, radiance, the light of the Guru's gyan. Asur = demons, the vices, lust and the rest. Sanghare = destroys.
(The person within whom) the light (of the gyan given by the Satguru) arises destroys lust and the other vices (within himself).
When the sun rises, the demons are slain;
When the sun of Divine comprehension rises, the mortal slays the demons,
When the sun of gyan rises, it destroys the asur, which are lust and the other vices.
1Y84: Uchau = the Hari who is highest of all. Sabad = through the Guru's Shabad.
By the blessing of the Satguru's Shabad he has the vision of the Supreme Purakh, and (then that person) reflects (thus: that)
the mortal looks upwards, and contemplates the Shabad.
looks upwards and deliberates on the Name.
That person, reflecting on the Guru's Shabad, sees the high Parmesar. Where does he see Him?
5964: Aad ant = from beginning to end, as long as the world lasts. Tihu loi = in the three worlds, in the whole world.
as long as creation lasts, that Parmatma Himself is (the protector) over (everyone's head) in the whole world,
The Lord is beyond the beginning and the end, beyond the three worlds.
In the high and low, beginning and the end and the three worlds he then sees the one Lord.
He is above, (aad ant) forever, in the three (loi) worlds — Parmeshvar, the one who gives light.
UGZZ: Aape = Himself alone. Soi = that Parmatma alone.
He Himself (pervading all beings) does the work, speaks and hears,
He Himself acts, speaks and listens.
That Lord Himself does, utters and hears all.
He Himself is the maker of the Vedas; He Himself, becoming the Pandit, expounds them, and He Himself, becoming the listener, hears them.
